original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Prove the exact 25-term arbitrary-positive destination-row price envelope for demand (1,2,4) over F2^3, with matching words; extend to nonzero pairwise orthogonal triples over Boolean rings. No complete Pareto census is claimed.
scope_change_reason: Explicit donor assignment of Open next question 2 from #5304; an algebraic side result, not an H2/K replacement or a physical supplier expansion.
bottleneck_link: An exact abstract dirty-input bill; physical access, routing, precision, stock and complete supplier admission remain separate. No new kappa.
stop_rule: Prove the sharp one-insertion bound and complete multi-insertion price envelope; otherwise publish the exact unresolved branch. Bound finite corroboration to small Boolean rings and representative independent shortest paths.
evidence: README.md supplies an all-word proof. The self-contained verifier checks 456 demands, 11400 words, 91200 formal forward/inverse column checks, 204800 literal input checks, 25 strictly exposed terms, 81 independent weighted column distances, ten controls, and five full-state shortest paths settling 90347 states. Finite evidence is not proof-kernel or independent human acceptance. Registered normal/optimized Python 3.12 replays agree; three disposable optimized-mode mutations reject underpricing, an omitted suffix gate and incorrectly tying the extra ADD destination to the insertion root.
author: lee-phys, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in source inspection, mathematical derivation, implementation, exact experiments, verification and writing; no subagents or independent reviewers.

open_questions.question: What is the complete aggregate Pareto frontier for (1,2,4) over F2^3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact price envelope need not enumerate unexposed componentwise minimal count vectors.
open_questions.first_step: Test eight-ADD single-insertion words with incoming counts (3,3,2) and its permutations, allowing any insertion root and all original dirt columns.
open_questions.blocked_by: The weighted prefix/suffix bound permits these counts but does not construct or exclude them.

open_questions.question: What is the exact tariff for the same demand with independent directed-edge prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Destination-only prices do not model arbitrary routing asymmetry.
open_questions.first_step: Use common source price, unit prices on a directed three-cycle, and one common positive reverse-edge price; preserve the full dirt matrix.
open_questions.blocked_by: The column proof charges destinations rather than parents; the return lemma is not a universal per-edge bound.
